text:
Wei Chen: hey @Elliot Price quick Q coming out of the checklist deep-link work — can we standardize UTM conventions for Console -> docs links? want to be able to attribute “conversion” back to checklist step (at least doc click-through + downstream first success).

Wei Chen: right now we have a bunch of links in copy drafts like `/docs/quickstart` but no params. design asked for a convention + what the canonical fields are.

Elliot Price: yep, we need this. also want to avoid random params per team. @Kenji Nakamura what did you all assume in the UX spec?

Kenji Nakamura: in spec we just noted “add UTM tags for attribution” + “version-stable docs URLs” (no hardcoded `/latest/`). didn’t prescribe exact params. we can implement whatever docs wants as long as it’s consistent.

Marissa Cole: +1. also note we’ll be shipping this behind a flag first, so we can test attribution before GA. needs to work for sidebar and the empty-state CTAs.

Elliot Price: proposal:
- Always include `utm_source=console`
- `utm_medium=onboarding_checklist` (or `console_checklist`?)
- `utm_campaign=guided_onboarding` (optionally include year/month)
- Add a Redwood-specific param for step attribution: `onboarding_step=<step_id>`

Elliot Price: I’d rather not overload utm_content with internal IDs, but we could if analytics prefers.

Nadia Rahman: jumping in — we can ingest UTMs as-is on the docs side (GA) but for our internal event pipeline we should be explicit. Also: we need to be careful about adding any identifiers that could be considered personal data. `onboarding_step` is fine. please do NOT include org/project ids in querystring.

Logan Wright: from analytics platform POV, UTMs are okay for web analytics, but we still need the Console -> docs click event in our pipeline to connect step completion. i.e., parse query param on docs page view alone won’t link back unless we join on something.

Logan Wright: best path IMO:
1) Console emits `onboarding_docs_link_clicked` with `step_id`, `doc_path`, `destination_url` (without any secrets)
2) Docs site emits `docs_page_viewed` with a whitelisted `utm_*` + `onboarding_step` (if present)
3) We can do aggregate attribution on the docs side, but “conversion to first success” still anchored on Console/backend events.

Mei Lin: +1 to (1). otherwise we’re stuck doing fuzzy joins on time window. if we have click event w/ step_id we can build funnel: checklist step -> docs click -> return to console -> completed.

Jean-Paul Laurent: copy question: do we want the params visible? some folks get suspicious when they see long URLs.

Elliot Price: fair. but UTM params are pretty standard. we can keep it short.

Kenji Nakamura: UX note: in Console we show link preview on hover sometimes; long URLs look messy. we can keep to 3 UTMs + 1 step param.

Marissa Cole: can we align naming with other Console docs links? i think growth uses `utm_source=console` already but medium varies.

Elliot Price: yeah I’ll check what’s already in prod. but for checklist, medium should be stable so dashboards don’t get messy.

Nadia Rahman: +1. also please ensure the docs site ignores unknown params (it will), but for internal event schema we should explicitly allowlist these params so we don’t accidentally capture random stuff.

Wei Chen: step_id naming: do we have a canonical list? current drafts have human titles (“Make first request”, “Handle 429s”).

Marissa Cole: PM side we’re moving to stable IDs in PRD/UX spec. examples: `api_key_created`, `first_request_success`, `first_streaming_session`, `usage_dashboard_visit`, `rate_limits_quota_read`, `prod_key_created`, `first_prod_launch_reviewed`.

Elliot Price: perfect. if those IDs exist, we should use them everywhere (Console step state, docs anchors, analytics).

Logan Wright: would recommend `onboarding_step_id` instead of `onboarding_step` to avoid future ambiguity.

Elliot Price: works for me.

Mei Lin: can we also include `utm_content=<step_id>` and skip custom param? GA tooling is a bit happier w/ standard utm fields.

Nadia Rahman: either is fine. but remember `utm_content` can be used by marketing elsewhere. if we reuse it, mixing might happen.

Elliot Price: I’d rather keep:
- `utm_source=console`
- `utm_medium=onboarding_checklist`
- `utm_campaign=guided_onboarding_2026`
- `onboarding_step_id=<step_id>`

Elliot Price: Example:
`https://redwoodinference.com/docs/hosted-api/first-request?utm_source=console&utm_medium=onboarding_checklist&utm_campaign=guided_onboarding_2026&onboarding_step_id=first_request_success`

Kenji Nakamura: ok. we can implement a tiny helper in Console to build these consistently.

Marissa Cole: also needs to be compatible with versioned docs links we’re doing. i.e. some links might be `/docs/hosted-api/first-request` and we might add a `?ref=` later for docs versioning. shouldn’t collide.

Elliot Price: query params will merge fine. just don’t double-encode.

Wei Chen: how do we attribute “conversion back to checklist steps” exactly? is the ask just “docs click rates per step” or “docs click -> completed step”?

Mei Lin: both. but primary is “docs click-through per step” + whether clicking docs correlates with completion (esp for the sticky steps: retries/timeouts + rate limits).

Logan Wright: if we have the click event in Console, we can directly answer click-through. to answer “did clicking help?”, we can look at step completion within N hours after click. no need to stitch across domains.

Nadia Rahman: +1. also reduces privacy risk. cross-domain user stitching is the can of worms we don’t want in this project.

Jean-Paul Laurent: nice. for docs pages themselves, do we want to display “came from Console checklist” anywhere? prob not.

Elliot Price: nope.

Elliot Price: Action items:
- Elliot: write short “UTM + onboarding_step_id conventions” blurb for docs/console teams + add to the deep-link ticket
- Kenji: add helper / ensure design spec references the exact params
- Nadia/Logan: confirm allowlist on docs telemetry + confirm the Console click event name/properties

Marissa Cole: can we make it explicit that the step ID should be the *origin step* even if link points to generic landing page? otherwise we lose attribution.

Elliot Price: yep. step ID reflects where the user clicked from (checklist step), not the destination.

Wei Chen: cool. I’ll update the copy draft links once we have the final param names.

Nadia Rahman: last note: please avoid adding anything that looks like an API key in the URL (obvious, but we’ve seen “paste your key in query param” mistakes in the wild). maybe worth adding a lint/test.

Kenji Nakamura: :thumbsup: we can add a small unit test around the helper to ensure only known params are included.

Elliot Price: I’ll post the convention in this thread once I sanity check existing UTMs in Console.

Elliot Price: (later) checked prod Console docs links — they use `utm_source=console&utm_medium=product`. so we’ll keep `utm_source=console` consistent and use `utm_medium=onboarding_checklist` specifically for this feature. ok to proceed.

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: ship it.

Mei Lin: once this is live in beta cohort, ping me and I’ll add a quick dashboard cut for docs click-through by step_id.

Wei Chen: thanks all!
